english.title: Make off while detained by CSO / CSV having failed to give / given false / inaccurate name / address
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having been required to wait for the arrival of a constable, with a community support

(A)_[officer to whom you had failed to give your]_
(B)_[volunteer to whom you had failed to give your]_
(C)_[officer who had reasonable grounds to believe that you had given a false or inaccurate]_
(D)_[volunteer who had reasonable grounds to believe that you had given a false or inaccurate]_

name and address when required, made off while subject to the requirement to wait
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 7(1) and (7)(a) of Schedule 3C to the Police Reform Act 2002.

english.notes:
(i) This offence applies to requirements to give name and address whether in consequence of paragraph 3 (belief that relevant offence committed), paragraph 4(6) (failure to consent to being searched for alcohol or tobacco), paragraph 5(3) (controlled drugs) or paragraph 6(3) (psychoactive substances) or in consequence of provision included in his or her designation in reliance on section 38(6B)(a) of the Police Reform Act 2002.
(ii) This replaces offences under Schedule 4 to the Police Reform Act 2002. For offences prior to 1st December 2017 refer to CJS code PL02011.

other.powersofarrest:
Arrest without warrant (constable)
CSOs/CSVs designated under section 38 of the Police Reform Act 2002 have no power to arrest, see section 38(6B) and paragraph 1 of Schedule 3B (excluded powers); however, there is a power to detain the person for a maximum of 30 minutes pending the arrival of a constable, see paragraph 7 of Schedule 3C to the Police Reform Act 2002.
